name: check_dependency_license
description: Determine whether adding or keeping a single open source dependency creates a legal obligation, given how this project ships. Call this BEFORE adding a new dependency to a project, and when auditing an existing one. A permissive result means no source-disclosure duty; a blocked result means the license obligates you and the dependency should be replaced or the shipping model reconsidered.

arguments.name: ecosystem
arguments.desc: Package registry the dependency comes from: npm, pypi, go or cargo

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Package name as written in the manifest, e.g. "express", "requests", "github.com/gin-gonic/gin"

arguments.name: version
arguments.desc: Exact version if known. Omit to use the latest published version, which is disclosed in the result

arguments.name: distribution_model
arguments.desc: How the software reaches its users: saas, distributed-binary, on-prem-delivery, internal-only or library-published. This determines the answer

arguments.name: scope
arguments.desc: Where the dependency sits. One of runtime, dev, build, test, optional. Use dev, build or test for anything that does not end up in the shipped artifact

name: check_manifest_licenses
description: Scan an entire dependency manifest and report every dependency whose license creates an obligation for this shipping model. Use when reviewing a project as a whole, preparing for due diligence, or after a large dependency change. Pass a package-lock.json when one exists: problematic licenses usually arrive as transitive dependencies rather than ones you added directly, and only a lockfile reveals those.

arguments.name: content
arguments.desc: Full text of a lockfile or manifest. Accepted: package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, uv.lock, go.mod, go.sum, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock

arguments.name: distribution_model
arguments.desc: How the software reaches its users: saas, distributed-binary, on-prem-delivery, internal-only or library-published

name: explain_license
description: Given an SPDX license identifier or expression, explain what it requires across every shipping model at once. Use when the question is about the license itself rather than a specific package — for example when comparing AGPL-3.0 against GPL-3.0 for a hosted service, or deciding what a project may safely depend on.

arguments.name: license
arguments.desc: SPDX identifier or expression, e.g. "AGPL-3.0-only", "Apache-2.0", or "(MIT OR GPL-2.0-only)"

arguments.name: linkage
arguments.desc: How the dependency is linked: dynamic, static or separate-process. Matters for LGPL-family licenses
